Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the invite. I tried to open the calendar invitation but the "Join" button is not showing up for several members of my team in Google Calendar. The description contains a link, but when we click it the browser drops us to an internal redirect page and then 404s.

We run strict CSP and some tenants route calendar link rendering differently; several folks are remote and rely on the embedded join button. Can we either: (1) resend as a Zoom invite with host controls, or (2) provide a one-click fallback URL that isn't embedded in the ICS?

Also, Anita is on a laptop that blocks external calendar scripts — she can't see the attachment preview.

Appreciate a quick fix — we still want to keep the 3pm slot if possible.

Subject: Fwd: Join button missing — suggested workaround

Kim / Laura — forwarding Samir's note. Quick technical summary and proposal:

- Symptom: ICS contains an anchor that some GCal clients render as a stripped HTML blob; embedded Join UI is not produced.
- Impact: Attendees see either (a) raw link that 404s due to our shortlink redirect, or (b) no join at all when client blocks preview.

Remediation options I recommend (in order):
1) Ephemeral host Zoom meeting: provision a temporary Zoom meeting for this session with host auth pinned to our moderator. Send a fresh ICS containing Zoom's join URL in both the description and the LOCATION field (helps Gmail/GCal surface the button).
2) Add a raw fallback URL in the first line of the invite description (explicit https://zoom.us/j/...), and include a short passcode in the invite body.
3) Re-issue calendar invite rather than forwarding — that ensures organizer header and join metadata are owned by the new meeting resource.

I can create the Zoom meeting and produce a new ICS. Will also attach a one-page join instructions snippet for AcmeCorp IT (for Anita's laptop).

Planned attachments: acme-zoom-invite.ics (text/calendar), join-instructions.txt (text/plain)

If OK, Kimberly, I'll spin this up now and we can keep 3:00pm ET.

—Ben
